digest.component_or_area: config-ownership AST gate and approved-seam registry
propositions: No gate currently proves that ONLY approved composition roots and provider boundaries read ambient config and credentials; new below-seam load_config/os.getenv reads or unowned credentials can silently appear.

An AST gate check_config_ownership.py must detect six prohibited access categories (ambient env reads, helper-shim reads, load_config calls, getattr env equivalents, provider-credential reads outside boundary, configurable adapter defaults/backend reloads) and fail CLOSED on unresolved dynamic reads and shim-shaped callees absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS.

The owner registry must derive credential names from _child_env.owned_secret_names(), backend keys from static @register decorator scans (not import-time-empty _REGISTRY), and env baseline from gen_env_registry.scan + _deprecations.REGISTRY, with distinct provider-credential vs composition-root seam sets.

Alias and receiver-object resolution must handle callee aliases (import-as, from-import, local assignment) and receiver bindings (os.environ directly or conditionally) to close evasions like src=os.environ; src.get(SECRET).
The gate must structurally reject path-glob exceptions and require exact path+symbol+rationale entries for all legacy-exception entries, which C3 will drain to empty.

The script must expose check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int contract, run offline with no CI/network, exit 0 on the current tree (legacy-exception set covers current reads), and include synthetic fixtures for each of six categories plus self-tests for path-globs, unowned names, and missing rationales.
